concept: MLX allocator memory limit GC limit and buffer cache
summary: Resource count cap: malloc throws "[metal::malloc] Resource limit (N) exceeded." when the number of live Metal resources reaches the device resource limit, after trying to reclaim cache.

facts.text: Resource count cap: malloc throws "[metal::malloc] Resource limit (N) exceeded." when the number of live Metal resources reaches the device resource limit, after trying to reclaim cache.
max buffer: sizes above device maxBufferLength throw a dedicated message.
set_wired_limit throws if the limit exceeds max_recommended_working_set_size.
Reported fragmentation: one user blames the buffer cache for a SIGABRT after about 14 hours (issue 1015), but this is a single unverified report.

Docs for set_cache_limit say the cache limit defaults to the memory limit. In source, max_pool_size_ is initialized to block_limit_ at construction, and set_memory_limit changes block_limit_ and gc_limit_ but not max_pool_size_. After a set_memory_limit call the two diverge. Both sides stated as read; not averaged.
Whether the issue 1015 fragmentation claim is real: MLX buffers are exact page-multiple sizes cached by size, so same-size reuse is the only reuse path.
The device resource_limit value on Apple silicon (not in the fetched pages).
MetalAllocator initializes block_limit_ = min(1.5 x max_recommended_working_set_size, 0.95 x memory_size), gc_limit_ = min(0.95 x max_recommended, block_limit_), and max_pool_size_ = block_limit_.
set_memory_limit swaps block_limit_ and recomputes gc_limit_ = min(block_limit_, 0.95 x recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize) but leaves max_pool_size_ unchanged.
set_cache_limit only swaps max_pool_size_ and returns the old value.
The set_cache_limit doc says free memory is reclaimed from the cache on the next allocation and that a limit of 0 disables the cache.
malloc rounds sizes above vm_page_size up to a whole page multiple before looking in the cache.
On a cache miss malloc computes mem_required = active + cache + size and, if it is at least gc_limit_ or the resource count is at the limit, releases cached buffers worth mem_required - gc_limit_.
Buffers smaller than 256 bytes are taken from a 1 MiB MTL heap (small_size_ = 256, heap_size_ = 1 << 20); the heap is skipped on the "Apple Paravirtual device" VM.
malloc throws "[metal::malloc] Resource limit (N) exceeded." when num_resources_ >= resource_limit_ after reclaiming.
malloc throws a dedicated error when a request exceeds device maxBufferLength.
free() recycles the buffer into the cache only while cache memory is below max_pool_size_; otherwise it erases the buffer from the residency sets and releases it.
Every non-heap buffer is inserted into the residency set on creation and erased on release, so cached buffers stay resident until released.
make_buffer wraps existing memory with device newBuffer(ptr, size, options, nullptr), inserts it into the residency set and counts it in active memory; release() frees it without caching.
All MLX Metal buffers use shared storage mode with untracked hazard tracking.
set_wired_limit throws std::invalid_argument when the limit exceeds max_recommended_working_set_size.
The global allocator is heap-allocated and never destroyed, so cached buffers are leaked at exit on purpose to save exit time.

mlx-lm issue 1015 (opened 2026-03-17) reports generate() terminating the process with "[METAL] Command buffer execution failed: Insufficient Memory (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)" and no recovery path.

The 1015 reporter attributes a SIGABRT after about 14 hours at 50 requests/hour on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit to cache fragmentation, and works around it with mx.clear_cache(), gc.collect(), set_memory_limit/set_cache_limit, and process recycling every 24 hours.

Because buffers are page-multiple sized and reused only by size, a long-running server with varied prompt lengths can hold many unreusable cached sizes until the cache limit or gc_limit_ forces release.
CONTRADICTS (docs vs source, no existing file): the set_cache_limit doc says the cache limit defaults to the memory limit; in source this holds only until set_memory_limit is called.
